+Issue: [Start and test the frontend independently of backend services](https://github.com/dystrophyless/dubbed.ai/issues/67). Reviewer: **GPT-6.1 Sol, High**. +## Findings
+
+### QA-67-01 — MEDIUM — Storage startup only handles missing API, not denied access/open failure
+
+**Classification:** confirmed implementation robustness defect under controlled capability fault; associated requirements gap. **Affected boundary:** startup/capability fallback adjacent to AC-01 and the mock persistence seam with #73. The four issue AC do not explicitly require a denied-storage test, so this is not represented as a contradiction of the clean-startup clause.
+
+**Reproduce:** use the included `capture.cjs` on the mock server. Its `storage-denied-en-desktop` case installs an IndexedDB getter that throws `DOMException('Storage access denied', 'SecurityError')` before app modules execute. The body remains empty and Playwright captures the page error. The `storage-open-denied-en-desktop` case leaves a factory object present but makes `open()` throw the same DOMException; the landing mounts, with an unhandled promise rejection. These are deliberate fault injections; no claim is made that the ordinary inspected localhost browser blocks storage or that the exact getter fault is common.
+
+**Expected:** the existing localized storage-unavailable explanation should cover unusable storage as well as an absent API. **Actual:** missing API shows guidance; thrown access is rethrown and leaves a white viewport, while failed open is not incorporated into startup readiness.
+
+**Source/cause:** [services/index.ts:55](/D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/services/index.ts:55) reads the global API and checks only falsiness, then stores `openWorkspaceDatabase(...)` as a promise at line61. [indexeddb.ts:35](/D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/services/indexeddb.ts:35) performs `factory.open` inside that promise. [main.tsx:33](/D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/main.tsx:33) catches only three typed synchronous errors and rethrows others at line41; it does not await database readiness. [RuntimeFailure.tsx:9](/D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/app/RuntimeFailure.tsx:9) already provides the storage variant.
+
+**Impact:** in an environment denying storage, a reviewer/user may receive no recovery guidance, or see a plausible start screen before persistent operations can work. This wastes debugging effort and masks the prerequisite for the local mock. Ordinary startup succeeds, so severity is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.
+
+**Scoped recommendation:** normalize storage access/open failure into the existing typed storage-unavailable state and account for initial database readiness. Coordinate bootstrap ownership with the persistent-mock owner; do not add a storage-repair subsystem. Extend the runtime task's failure contract with absent API, denied access and failed open, preserving existing user data. **Next validation:** focused assertions for all three cases, visible localized recovery text, no uncaught errors, and a restored normal smoke pass.
+
+Blank body under injected getter denial:
+
+![Controlled IndexedDB access denial: blank1440x900 viewport](evidence/storage-denied-en-desktop.png)
+
+The existing useful absent-API state, which should be reused:
+
+![Missing IndexedDB: readable localized recovery guidance](evidence/storage-absent-ru-phone.png)
+
+Open failure still presents the landing; the screenshot alone cannot prove the technical fault. `metrics-extra.json` records the associated `Storage access denied` page error, and the owned Vite process logged an unhandled rejection.
+
+![Controlled IndexedDB open failure leaves normal landing visible](evidence/storage-open-denied-en-desktop.png)
+
+### QA-67-02 — LOW — Shared compact-desktop rule makes important form actions unnecessarily small
+
+**Classification:** requirement/design flaw; cross-owner observation for shared tokens/shell #78 and the relevant screen owners. **Not an implementation mismatch or an additional UI responsibility for #67.** A compact button is not automatically an accessibility violation.
+
+**Reproduce/measure:** open sign-in at1440px or768px, then767px in RU. After `document.fonts.ready`, the desktop primary Sign in is **28px high with13/20 text**, Show password **24px with12/16 text**. At767px the actions are **48px with16/24 text**. The landing's desktop Start dubbing is **110x32px,13/20**, despite abundant whitespace. See `metrics.json` and `metrics-extra.json` for DOM values and geometry.
+
+**Expected quality:** primary entry actions for casual users should be easy to find/read and comfortably acquire; desktop pointer use does not require mobile density, but sparse screens do not benefit much from extreme compression. **Actual:** the sign-in action is visually shorter than its40px email/password fields, and the large-to-compact jump occurs across a single pixel at767/768. The reference treatment is preserved, yet hierarchy and readability weaken on the desktop composition.
+
+**Source/cause:** the adopted source explicitly selects24/28/32 heights and12/13 labels. [App.css:306](/D:/Program/python/Dubbed/frontend/src/App.css:306) and size rules at337–351 implement them; phone rules restore48/16. This is faithful to current tokens and the Clean source, so the underlying requirement deserves reconsideration. It should not be fixed ad hoc in runtime tooling.
+
+**Impact/interpretation:** small labels/actions are less prominent in a form that is the user's main job; source fidelity alone does not establish an optimal task-specific size. No measured click-error rate or formal target-size violation is claimed.
+
+**Scoped recommendation:** retain Mabry, palette,6px radius and Clean states, while reviewing a larger desktop role for primary entry/form actions (for example36–40px and14–16px labels), keeping compact variants for genuinely dense secondary controls. **Next validation:** compare original/proposed EN/RU desktop and short-height screenshots, keyboard focus,200% browser zoom and pointer acquisition. Require an explicit shared design decision before changing tokens.

A foundation task has no own dialog/interaction layout; screen-specific states remain with their reviewers. Network observations are limited to captured visits and the focused smoke, not a universal transport audit. Browser-storage fault cases were synthetic; native browser-policy reproduction remains the next robustness validation. Historical `foundation-cohort-acceptance.md`/clean-install receipts explain prior acceptance and are not presented as fresh checks.
